# ataila_feedback_item (Data Source)

One Feedback & Roadmap item in full: the report, the screen it was filed from, what the reporter's installation ran, the thread (internal notes included) and every move of its planned week. Answers only on the platform that issues releases (elsewhere `feedback_unavailable`), to a token holding `feedback-admin-global`, from platform release 1.0.260 on. Read-only: the provider never fetches an item's brief, which would move the item to `in_progress`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# One item in full, with its thread. Reading it never fetches the brief, so the
# item's status does not change.
data "ataila_feedback_item" "item" {
  number = 41
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `number` (Number) The item's number, `N` of `#N`.

### Read-Only

- `acceptance_criteria` (String) What is true once the work is done, one statement per line; null until written.
- `auto_close_at` (String) When a delivered item closes by itself unless the reporter reopens it. RFC 3339 in UTC.
- `body` (String) The report itself (Markdown), as the reporter wrote it.
- `comments` (Attributes List) The thread, oldest first. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--comments))
- `confirmed_at` (String) When the reporter confirmed that it works. RFC 3339 in UTC.
- `context` (Attributes) What the reporter's installation was running. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--context))
- `created_at` (String) When it was filed. RFC 3339 in UTC.
- `customer_key` (String) The customer the item belongs to (its stable key).
- `customer_label` (String) The customer's name.
- `delivered_at` (String) When it became `delivered`. RFC 3339 in UTC.
- `delivered_build` (String) The production build that carries the change (set when it becomes `ready`).
- `delivered_release_id` (String) That release's id, e.g. `2026.10.4`.
- `delivered_release_seq` (Number) The sequence number of the release that ships it; null until that release is published.
- `duplicate_of_number` (Number) For a `duplicate`, the number of the item it duplicates; null otherwise.
- `expected_week` (String) The ISO week the work is planned for (`2026-W43`); null until scheduled.
- `kind` (String) What it asks for: `blocker_bug`, `change` (a change request) or `new_feature`.
- `lang` (String) The language of the report: `en` or `hu`.
- `page` (Attributes) The screen it was filed from. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--page))
- `planned_release_id` (String) The release it is planned for, if any.
- `public_title` (String) The title release notes print, when one was set at triage; null = the title.
- `ready_at` (String) When it became `ready`. RFC 3339 in UTC.
- `released_at` (String) When the release that ships it was published. RFC 3339 in UTC.
- `severity` (String) For a bug: `blocker`, `major` or `minor`; null for the other kinds.
- `source` (String) Where it was filed: `internal` (on this platform by its own staff), `island` (on a customer installation) or `demo` (on a demo installation: a lead signal).
- `status` (String) Where the item is: `new`, `triaged`, `scheduled` (has an expected week), `in_progress`, `ready` (built into a production build of the platform, not yet installed where it was reported), `delivered` (the release that carries it is installed there), `closed`; or one of the terminal `rejected` (see `status_reason`), `duplicate` (see `duplicate_of_number`) and `withdrawn`.
- `status_reason` (String) The reason given with a rejection or a withdrawal; null otherwise.
- `submitter_name` (String) Who filed it, as their name was known then.
- `summary_en` (String) An English summary of an item reported in another language; null for an English report or until it is written.
- `ticket_url` (String) A linked helpdesk ticket, if any.
- `title` (String) The title as the reporter wrote it.
- `updated_at` (String) When it last changed. RFC 3339 in UTC.
- `votes` (Number) Upvotes, every side together.
- `week_history` (Attributes List) Every move of the expected week, oldest first; empty when it never moved. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--week_history))

<a id="nestedatt--comments"></a>
### Nested Schema for `comments`

Read-Only:

- `author_name` (String) Who wrote it, as their name was known then.
- `body` (String) The message (Markdown).
- `created_at` (String) When it was filed. RFC 3339 in UTC.
- `internal` (Boolean) True for a vendor-side internal note: never shown to the customer.
- `lang` (String) Its language: `en` or `hu`.
- `side` (String) `customer` (the reporter's side) or `ataila` (the vendor's).


<a id="nestedatt--context"></a>
### Nested Schema for `context`

Read-Only:

- `browser` (String) The reporter's browser.
- `build` (String) The platform build, e.g. `1.0.258`.
- `edition` (String) The installation's edition.
- `locale` (String) The interface language, `en` or `hu`.
- `release_id` (String) The installed release, e.g. `2026.10.3`.
- `release_seq` (Number) The installed release's sequence number.
- `viewport` (String) The browser window size, e.g. `1920x1080`.


<a id="nestedatt--page"></a>
### Nested Schema for `page`

Read-Only:

- `key` (String) The page's navigation key, e.g. `projects`.
- `route` (String) The page's path at the time, e.g. `/projects/12`.
- `title` (String) The page's title at the time.


<a id="nestedatt--week_history"></a>
### Nested Schema for `week_history`

Read-Only:

- `at` (String) RFC 3339 in UTC.
- `previous_week` (String) The ISO week it was planned for, `2026-W42`.
- `reason` (String) Why it moved, as the customer was told.
- `week` (String) The ISO week it moved to.
